summary: Accessibility Bugs - AP Registration Page (WCAG 2.1 AA Violations)

bugs.title: [A11Y] AP Registration - Missing aria-describedby and aria-invalid on form fields with errors
bugs.description: h3. Summary Form fields on the AP Registration page do not use `aria-describedby` or `aria-invalid` attributes when validation errors occur. Screen reader users cannot identify which fields have errors or what the error messages say. h3. Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://hub-ui-admin-qa.swarajability.org/partner-registration 2. Enter an invalid email (e.g., "invalid-email") in the Official Email ID field 3. Move focus away from the field (blur) 4. Inspect the field's ARIA attributes h3. Expected Result - Field should have `aria-invalid="true"` when input is invalid - Field should have `aria-describedby` pointing to the error message element ID - Screen readers should announce the error when the field receives focus h3. Actual Result - No `aria-invalid` attribute is set on the field - No `aria-describedby` attribute links the field to any error message - Screen reader users have no way to know the field has an error h3. WCAG Reference - *3.3.1 Error Identification (Level A)*: If an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text. - *4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)*: States and properties must be programmatically determinable. h3. Impact Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) cannot identify form errors, making registration impossible without sighted assistance. h3. Suggested Fix {code:html} Please enter a valid email address {code}
bugs.acceptanceCriteria:
- All required fields set aria-invalid="true" when validation fails
- All error messages linked via aria-describedby
- Screen readers announce errors when field receives focus

bugs.title: [A11Y] AP Registration - No aria-live region for OTP dynamic content announcement
bugs.description:
h3. Summary When a user clicks "Send OTP to email", the OTP input field and Verify button appear dynamically on the page. However, there is no `aria-live` region to announce this change to screen reader users. They have no way to know new content has appeared without manually navigating the page. h3. Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://hub-ui-admin-qa.swarajability.org/partner-registration 2. Enter a valid email in the Official Email ID field 3. Click "Send OTP to email" button 4. Observe that OTP input field and Verify button appear 5. Check for aria-live regions in the DOM h3. Expected Result - An `aria-live="polite"` or `role="status"` region should announce "OTP sent to your email" or similar - The appearance of the OTP input field should be communicated to assistive technology - Screen reader users should be informed without needing to manually search the page h3. Actual Result - No `aria-live` region exists on the page - OTP field appears silently - Screen reader users are unaware that new interactive content has appeared - Similarly, verification success ("Verified ✓") is not announced h3. WCAG Reference - *4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA)*: Status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus. h3. Impact Screen reader users cannot complete the OTP verification flow independently because they don't know when the OTP field appears or when verification succeeds. h3. Suggested Fix {code:html}

OTP has been sent to your email

Email verified successfully {code}
bugs.acceptanceCriteria:
- aria-live="polite" region announces OTP sent status
- OTP field appearance is communicated to screen readers
- Verification success/failure announced via aria-live or role="status"
- No focus steal - announcements happen without moving focus

bugs.title: [A11Y] AP Registration - Missing autocomplete attributes on email and phone fields
bugs.description:
h3. Summary
The Official Email ID and Phone Number fields on the AP Registration page are missing `autocomplete` attributes. This prevents browsers and assistive technologies from auto-filling these fields, which is especially important for users with motor disabilities or cognitive impairments.

h3. Steps to Reproduce
1. Navigate to https://hub-ui-admin-qa.swarajability.org/partner-registration
2. Inspect the Official Email ID input element
3. Inspect the Phone Number input element
4. Check for `autocomplete` attribute on both

h3. Expected Result
- Email field should have `autocomplete="email"`
- Phone field should have `autocomplete="tel"`
- Password field should have `autocomplete="new-password"`
- Organization name could have `autocomplete="organization"`

h3. Actual Result
- Email field: no `autocomplete` attribute
- Phone field: no `autocomplete` attribute
- Browser console shows: "Input elements should have autocomplete attributes (suggested: current-password)"

h3. WCAG Reference
- *1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (Level AA)*: The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined when the input field serves a purpose identified in the Input Purposes for User Interface Components section.

h3. Impact
Users with motor disabilities who rely on autofill cannot automatically populate these fields. Users with cognitive disabilities lose the benefit of browser-assisted form filling.

h3. Suggested Fix
{code:html}
<input type="email" autocomplete="email" name="email" />
<input type="tel" autocomplete="tel" name="phone" />
<input type="password" autocomplete="new-password" name="password" />
{code}
bugs.acceptanceCriteria:
- Email field has autocomplete="email"
- Phone field has autocomplete="tel"
- Password field has autocomplete="new-password"
- Browser autofill works correctly for these fields

bugs.title: [A11Y] AP Registration - Form element missing accessible name (aria-label/aria-labelledby)
bugs.description:
h3. Summary The `
` element on the AP Registration page has no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` attribute. Screen reader users navigating by landmarks cannot identify the purpose of the form. h3. Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to https://hub-ui-admin-qa.swarajability.org/partner-registration 2. Use a screen reader to list form landmarks (NVDA: Insert+F7, JAWS: Insert+F5) 3. Observe the form is listed without a descriptive name h3. Expected Result - Form should be announced as "Assistive Partner Registration form" or similar - Screen reader landmark navigation should show a descriptive form name - The form should have `aria-labelledby` pointing to the "Partner Details" heading, or an `aria-label` h3. Actual Result - Form element exists but has no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` - Screen readers announce it generically as "form" without purpose - Users navigating by landmarks cannot distinguish this form from others h3. WCAG Reference - *4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)*: For all user interface components, the name and role can be programmatically determined. h3. Impact Screen reader users navigating by landmarks cannot identify the form's purpose, making it harder to orient on the page. h3. Suggested Fix {code:html}

Partner Details

...
...
{code}
bugs.acceptanceCriteria:
- Form element has aria-label or aria-labelledby
- Screen readers announce form purpose when navigating by landmarks
- Form name is descriptive and matches the page context
